This AVC RIG Camper Van Keeps Things Open and Roomy While Hiding a Shower in Plain Sight
22 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / AVC RIG
Today's featured build is based on a 2025 Ford Transit High Roof Extended. It was brought to life by AVC RIG, a Loveland, Colorado-based company that specializes in van conversion kits and full camper van conversions. We've covered some of its work here on autoevolution, such as this versatile setup . AVC stands for Adventure Van Conversions.
As usual, let's first take a look at the exterior. Although it doesn't have that many exterior mods like we see on other rigs, someone who's familiar with camper vans will be able to tell that it's a mobile home.
The van rides on black Transit alloy wheels wrapped in all-terrain tires. Moreover, on the sides, you'll notice an AM Auto window and two CR Laurence half-slider windows.
The last important upgrades are on the roof. There's an AVC rack that holds a solar panel and a flat-mounted Starlink antenna. Furthermore, the roof integrates a Maxxair vent fan and a 48V A/C unit.
Other notable mods are power and water connections, an SAP port for the Starlink system, and side steps.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / AVC RIG Inside is where things become more interesting. As you enter, you'll notice that the interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. The open layout, the small number of overhead cabinets, and the overall arrangement of the interior areas make the space feel very roomy.
Regarding aesthetics, the customer opted for AVC grey felt wall kits, a fabric trim with a different grey tone, a white ceiling, 2tec2 flooring, and glossy Azure Blue cabinetry. The look is complemented by a bright white solid surface countertop and some black accents, like the cabinet and drawer handles.
The driver and passenger seats came from the factory mounted on swivel bases, so they can be turned around to face the back of the van. The passenger seat base hides an Espar heater that's tapped directly into the vehicle's fuel tank.
If you want to enjoy a meal or work on your laptop in the cabin, you can set up a small table by using a Lagun mount. What's more, between the seats, you'll find an AVC locker.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / AVC RIG Straight ahead as you step inside, you'll come across the kitchen. It features a multi-function oven, a deep stainless steel sink with a cover, a dual-burner induction stovetop, and an IndelB fridge with a freezer compartment.
A large overhead cabinet, a cabinet underneath the sink, and a cutlery drawer are available for storage.
What looks like a massive lower cabinet behind the driver's seat is, in fact, a bathroom. Lift its hinged top and you'll discover a cleverly built shower setup. There's also enough space to add a toilet inside it.
On the opposite side, by the sliding door, AVC RIG fitted a single-person bench that offers storage space. Behind it, there's a counter offering a bit of surface area and four decently sized drawers.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / AVC RIG It has a Tetravan sprayer with a mixer and a pan underneath that drains into a tank on the bottom part of the van. To complete the shower setup, you must attach a curtain to the ceiling.
The rear part of the living space is taken up by a sleeping arrangement. It's a twin-bed setup, with each bed being 26 inches (66 centimeters) wide and 80 inches (203 centimeters) long. Of course, the beds can double as benches.
You get window cubbies on each side of this space, which offer a bit of room for storing bits and bobs, and also provide USB charging points. Above, there's a 48V Velit 2000R A/C unit that can quickly cool off the entire interior. The customer also requested to have four speakers integrated into the ceiling – and AVC RIG delivered.
The beds are also where the rig's utility systems live. Power is inside the passenger-side bench – the rig's electrical heart is an EcoFlow system with a 5 kW capacity that can be expanded to 10 kW.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / AVC RIG As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 30-gallon (113-liter) freshwater tank installed over the wheel well, a 6-gallon (22-liter) water heater, and an under-mounted greywater tank. A small door on the rear part of the driver-side bed offers access to an outdoor shower system.
Finally, there are two Van Essential storage pockets attached to the inner part of the back doors. Furthermore, all the windows in the van come with shades from the same brand.
All in all, this custom creation by AVC RIG keeps an open, roomy feel while also packing a bunch of creature comforts that make it possible to travel off-grid – that's a combo that's hard to achieve.
Besides offering conversions, the company also sells conversion parts for multiple van models, including the Ford Transit and the Mercedes-Benz Sprinter. So, if you liked a specific component or setup in this rig, you might be able to find it on the company's website.
